enriched_description: Elongated streamlined body with hardened elytra displaying bright metallic coloration (iridescent green, bronze, or blue). Large prominent compound eyes occupying significant portion of head. Long slender cursorial legs adapted for rapid running. Distinctive white or cream-colored curvilinear markings on elytra surface. Large sickle-shaped mandibles visible at anterior. Body proportions: elongated thorax relative to abdomen. Six-jointed legs with tarsal claws for gripping surfaces. Filiform antennae segmented and mobile.

Compact hemispherical dome-shaped body with smooth glossy elytra. Bright saturated coloration (red, orange, or yellow) with distinct circular black spots distributed symmetrically across elytra surface. Short clubbed antennae. Black pronotum with characteristic white lateral markings. Legs relatively short and tucked beneath body. Size proportion: width nearly equal to length creating rounded silhouette. Six legs with small tarsal segments. Body surface highly reflective with polished appearance.

Flattened elongated-oval body with hard elytra displaying iridescent black or metallic bronze coloration. Parallel longitudinal striations (grooves) running along entire elytra surface. Prominent forward-projecting mandibles. Long cursorial legs with spiny tibiae adapted for ground locomotion. Filiform thread-like segmented antennae. Body surface with glossy sheen. Proportions: elongated body with thorax slightly narrower than abdomen. Six legs with well-developed femora. Dark uniform coloration with metallic reflections under light.

Elongated cylindrical body with hardened elytra. Extremely long filiform antennae extending beyond body length (often 1.5-2x body length), composed of numerous distinct segments. Variable coloration patterns including mottled browns, blacks, or banded patterns on elytra surface. Robust chewing mandibles. Legs moderately long with tarsal claws for gripping bark. Body surface texture ranging from smooth to punctate. Proportions: antennae length significantly exceeding body length is primary diagnostic feature. Six legs with segmented structure.

Oval to broadly rounded body with smooth elytra displaying bright aposematic coloration (yellow, green, orange, or metallic hues). Often with contrasting dark markings or bands on elytra. Short to moderate length antennae. Legs relatively short with tarsal segments adapted for clinging to foliage. Body surface may be smooth or finely punctate. Proportions: body width substantial relative to length creating broad oval silhouette. Six legs with adhesive capabilities. Coloration often mimics host plant leaves.

Robust compact ovoid body with hard glossy elytra in dark coloration (black or dark brown). Flattened spiny forelegs (fossorial) adapted for digging and manipulating dung balls. Lamellate plate-like antennal clubs. Body surface with smooth polished appearance. Legs robust with prominent spines on tibiae. Proportions: compact body with disproportionately large forelegs. Body shape optimized for rolling behavior. Six legs with specialized digging adaptations. Dark uniform coloration with subtle metallic sheen.

Large robust heavily-built body with hard elytra in dark brown or black coloration. Prominent cephalic horn(s) projecting anteriorly from head (more pronounced in males), often with secondary thoracic horn. Horn surface smooth and curved upward or forward. Lamellate antennal clubs. Legs robust with tibial spines. Body surface with matte to semi-glossy finish. Proportions: horn length can exceed body length in males. Body significantly larger than most beetles. Six thick legs with strong gripping capability. Overall heavily armored appearance.

Small compact body with distinctive elongated snout (rostrum) projecting anteriorly from head. Elbowed geniculate antennae arising from rostrum. Elytra often with textured surface including punctures, scales, or setae. Coloration typically cryptic (browns, grays, blacks) often with mottled or banded patterns. Legs relatively short. Proportions: rostrum length varies but is diagnostic feature, often one-third to one-half of body length. Six legs with tarsal claws. Body surface often covered with fine scales or hairs providing camouflage.

Compact body with single pair of membranous forewings with visible venation patterns. Reduced hindwings modified into small knobbed halteres (balancing organs) visible laterally. Large prominent compound eyes occupying majority of head surface. Short antennae with aristate bristle-like terminal segment. Body surface variable: may be hairy, glossy, or matte. Legs slender with pulvilli adhesive pads on tarsi. Proportions: wingspan typically 1.5-2x body length. Six legs with specialized landing adaptations. Wing transparency with dark venation.

Robust densely hairy pubescent body with characteristic black and yellow or white banding patterns on abdomen. Two pairs of membranous wings with visible venation, forewings larger than hindwings, wings often folded longitudinally at rest. Branched plumose body hairs adapted for pollen collection. Hind legs with specialized pollen baskets (corbiculae) - smooth concave surfaces surrounded by hairs. Elbowed antennae. Stinger visible at posterior abdomen in females. Proportions: body robust and laterally compressed, wings extending beyond abdomen when folded. Six legs with pollen-carrying adaptations.
